Degree arithmetic re-derived independently of the attempt. Packet/SRC-0004 give deg(W_f|_C)=2(2g-2+4·2)-4f=4g+12-4f; g=6 yields deg W_5=24+12-20=16, deg W_4=24+12-16=20. deg ω_C=10, so deg L=16-10=6. Obstruction degree deg(ω_C⊗W_f^∨(Γ))=2g-2-(4g+12-4f)+n=4f+n-2g-14; at (g,n)=(6,6): f=5 gives 20+6-12-14=0, f=4 gives 16+6-12-14=-4. Cross-check of internal consistency: the source degree formula forces deg(O_{P(E^∨)}(1)|_C)=2g-2+8, i.e. O(1)|_C≅ω_C⊗γ^*O(2) up to degree, whence W_5|_C≅ω_C^{⊗2}⊗γ^*O(-1) of degree 20-4=16, confirming 16 by a second route. The dualisation sign is the one the packet mandates (γ^*O(-5) from F^∨=O(-4)⊕O(-5)); the SRC-0004 excerpt's display 'W_{f_i}=O_{PE^∨}(2)⊗γ^*O(f_i)' is contradicted by its own next line 'deg(O(2)|_C⊗γ^*O(−f_i)|_C)', and the attempt correctly follows the packet's −f convention. Note the sign matters materially: with the opposite convention the larger-degree summand would be W_5 and the failure condition would read O(Γ)≅W_4⊗ω_C^{-1}. The attempt is on the correct side of exactly the trap the packet flags.

Claim (A). deg(ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=-4<0 for every effective Γ of degree 6, and a line bundle of negative degree on an integral projective curve has no nonzero global section. Geometric fibres of B^{bal} are smooth projective genus-6 curves, hence integral (a genus-6 curve is connected by convention, and a CE-tetragonal structure with γ_*O_C=O⊕E^∨ forces h^0(O_C)=1). The claim quantifies over all effective degree-six divisors, not only reduced ones, and the argument only uses the degree, so the quantifier is discharged.

Claim (B). deg(ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))=0; on an integral projective curve a degree-zero line bundle admits a nonzero section iff it is trivial, and ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ)≅O_C ⟺ O_C(Γ)≅W_5⊗ω_C^{-1}=L. Both directions are genuine (the 'only if' uses integrality; the 'if' is immediate). Methods list names this 'serre-duality-degree-zero-line-bundle-criterion', which is a mislabel — no Serre duality is used or needed — but the mathematics is correct.

Claim (C). Given W|_C=W_4|_C⊕W_5|_C on a geometric fibre (F splits on P^1_k for k algebraically closed, so the splitting exists fibrewise even if not relatively), H^0(ω_C⊗W^∨(Γ))=H^0(ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))⊕H^0(ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ)); by (A) the first summand vanishes, so nonvanishing ⟺ O_C(Γ)≅L. Adversarial note recorded rather than charged as a defect: Z^{geo} is *defined* in the theorem statement as the nonvanishing locus of that H^0, so (C) is close to definitional and cannot be wrong for the reason that the CE obstruction space might mis-model the actual evaluation map. That limits the lemma's content but not its truth, and the theorem statement makes no claim beyond what is proved.

Claim (D). The multiplicity-free locus in the relative degree-six effective-divisor space is the complement of the (closed, nonempty) discriminant, hence open; each fibre Sym^6(C) is irreducible with nonempty discriminant, so the open is dense and not closed — the attempt respects the packet's explicit instruction not to call it closed. Conf_6→(reduced open) is finite of degree 720, étale (distinct sections stay distinct), and S_6 acts simply transitively on geometric fibres, so it is an S_6-torsor. Two attacks tried and failed: (i) the torsor is étale-locally, not Zariski-locally, trivial — the theorem says 'finite étale S_6-torsor', which is correct, though Step 5's phrase 'principal S_6-bundle' would be false if read Zariski-locally; (ii) freeness could fail on coarse moduli with residual automorphisms — the attempt itself states the torsor on the stack of pairwise-distinct sections and flags the coarse-space caveat, so the stack/coarse distinction is handled rather than elided. Terminological slack: 'reduced-support' is used (in packet and attempt alike) to mean multiplicity-free; supports are reduced by definition, but both documents use it consistently.

Claim (E). Riemann–Roch on a smooth genus-6 fibre: χ(L)=deg L-g+1=6-6+1=1, so h^0(L)=1+h^1(L)≥1 and |L|≠∅; effective divisors D with O(D)≅L correspond bijectively to points of |L|, so the unordered residual incidence is fibrewise nonempty. Correct as stated. The stated claim is strictly weaker than nonemptiness of Z^{geo}⊂Conf_6, which requires a *reduced* member of |L|; the attempt does not claim the stronger statement and explicitly defers it (see finding candidate FC-REV0036-B).

The adversary checklist items concerning Poincaré duality, Tate twists, BM-versus-ordinary degree, Gysin/Künneth shifts, spectral-sequence differentials, semisimplification versus honest Hodge isomorphism, predicted motives, pure-Tate-to-tautological upgrades, and omitted stable pairs are all inapplicable: the theorem statement makes no cohomological, weight, or motivic assertion, and its closing sentence explicitly disclaims any Tate-type claim about W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q). FND-0001 is cited as ambient dictionary only and is not used in any proof step; no PD identification or twist is manipulated. Coefficients never enter (no cohomology is computed), so the integral-versus-rational attack is vacuous here. Blocked routes vcd-only-vanishing, undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex, point-count-without-degree-parity-separation, and forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown are genuinely unused: I found no vcd argument, no graph complex, no point count, and no use of M_{6,6}→M_{6,5} anywhere in the argument or claim graph.

finding_candidates.statement: Over B^{bal} the CE summand W_5, hence L=W_5⊗ω_{C/B}^{-1}, is canonical only fibrewise: relatively one gets the destabilising subbundle M⊂F with M|_fibre≅O(5) determined up to twist by a pullback from the base, and W=W_4⊕W_5 need not split relatively. All fibrewise/geometric-point statements are unaffected because γ^*p^*N is trivial on fibres, but any global relative construction — a determinantal/Fitting ideal for the rank drop, a relative Abel–Jacobi section, or a Gysin pushforward along Z — must first fix a normalisation of L or work with the twist as a Brauer-type ambiguity.

finding_candidates.statement: If the CE normalisation implicit in the packet degree formula is O_{P(E^∨)}(1)|_C≅ω_C⊗γ^*O_{P^1}(2) — which is forced up to degree by deg(W_f|_C)=2(2g-2+8)-4f — then W_5≅ω_C^{⊗2}⊗γ^*O(-1) and L≅ω_C(-D) with D=γ^*(pt) the g^1_4 divisor. Riemann–Roch then gives h^0(L)=h^0(O_C(D))+1, so h^0(L)=3 exactly when the tetragonal pencil is a genuine g^1_4, sharpening the theorem's h^0(L)≥1 to h^0(L)=3 and making |L| a P^2. parsed_artifact.strongest_attack: Strongest attack attempted: that L:=W_5⊗ω_{C/B}^{-1} is not a well-defined object over B^{bal}, so the preamble of the theorem is ill-posed and claims (B)–(D) quantify over a phantom. The balanced splitting F≅O_{P^1}(4)⊕O_{P^1}(5) is a fibrewise statement; relatively over B^{bal} there is in general no Zariski- or even étale-local splitting of F, only a canonical destabilising subbundle M⊂F with M|_fibre≅O(5), well-defined up to twist by a line bundle pulled back from B. Hence W_5 (the corresponding quotient of W=O(2)⊗γ^*F^∨) and therefore L are only defined up to tensoring by γ^*p^*N for N on B, and the direct-sum decomposition W=W_4⊕W_5 used in Step 4 need not exist as a global relative splitting. The attack fails against the stated theorem for two reasons I verified. First, every one of (A)–(E) is quantified over geometric fibres and geometric points; on a geometric fibre F does split, so W=W_4⊕W_5 and the summand decomposition of H^0 hold there. Second, the residual pullback ambiguity is invisible fibrewise: γ^*p^*N restricted to a fibre is trivial, so the isomorphism class of L on each fibre, and hence the conditions O_C(Γ)≅L, deg L=6 and χ(L)=1, are unambiguous. The attack therefore downgrades to a well-posedness caveat that becomes load-bearing only downstream, where a global relative L is needed for a determinantal/Fitting scheme structure or any Gysin pushforward (C66-COMP-RANK, C66-TATE-SUPPORT) — recorded as FC-REV0036-A. Secondary attacks tried and defeated: the γ^*O(-f) sign (the attempt lands on the packet-mandated side, and the SRC-0004 excerpt's own degree line resolves its internal typo in the attempt's favour); Zariski- versus étale-local triviality of the S_6-torsor (the theorem says 'finite étale', which is correct, even though Step 5's 'principal S_6-bundle' would be false read Zariski-locally); freeness of the S_6-action on coarse moduli with residual automorphisms (the attempt states the torsor on the stack and flags the coarse-space failure itself); and the entire Tate/PD/Künneth/spectral-sequence family of attacks, which is inert because the theorem asserts no cohomological content and explicitly disclaims the campaign target. The most substantive residual criticism is not an error but a limitation: (C) is near-definitional, since Z^{geo} is defined in the statement as the nonvanishing locus of the CE obstruction space, so the lemma identifies that locus without establishing that CE obstruction nonvanishing is the operative evaluation failure for the campaign — a question the theorem statement does not raise and which therefore cannot count against it.
parsed_artifact.theorem_statement: Let g=6 and let B^{bal} be any base carrying a smooth family of genus-6 curves with a balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl structure (relations bundle F≅O_{P^1}(4)⊕O_{P^1}(5)), universal curve π:C→B^{bal}, and CE line bundles W_f:=(O_{P(E^∨)}(2)⊗γ^*O_{P^1}(-f))|_C for f∈{4,5} (packet convention: W_5 is the f_2=5 summand of (O(2)⊗γ^*F^∨)|_C, not the O_{P^1}(5) summand of F). Write L:=W_5⊗ω_{C/B}^{-1}. Let Conf_6(C/B^{bal}) be the relative stack of six ordered pairwise-distinct sections, with associated relative divisor Γ, and let Z^{geo}⊂Conf_6 be the geometric evaluation-failure locus consisting of geometric points at which the CE obstruction space H^0(C,ω_C⊗W^∨(Γ)) is nonzero. Then: (A) for every geometric fibre and every effective degree-six divisor Γ one has deg(ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=−4, hence H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=0; (B) for every such Γ one has deg(ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))=0, and H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))≠0 if and only if O_C(Γ)≅L; (C) consequently Z^{geo} coincides set-theoretically with the Abel–Jacobi incidence locus I^{geo} of geometric points satisfying O_C(Γ)≅L; (D) the locus of reduced-support degree-six effective divisors in the relative effective-divisor space is open (not closed), and the forgetful map from Conf_6 to that reduced-support open is a finite étale S_6-torsor on the stack of pairwise-distinct sections, so the ordered reduced failure locus is the preimage of the reduced-support open of the residual incidence for L; (E) on every smooth geometric fibre, χ(L)=1, hence h^0(L)≥1, so the residual linear system |L| is nonempty and the unordered residual incidence is fibrewise nonempty. This identifies the geometric evaluation-failure locus for the balanced tetragonal CE geometry of packet C66-001-v3; it does not assert scheme-theoretic equality of Fitting/determinantal ideals with the Abel–Jacobi ideal, does not stratify by h^0(L), and does not claim Tate type of any contribution to W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q).
